Being brave means trying something even when you feel a little bit wobbly inside.

spreads.text: At the bottom of the garden, under the old apple tree, lived a small grey mouse called Mabel. She had soft round ears and a tail like a curl of string.
spreads.sceneSummary: Mabel outside her home under the apple tree at sunset.

spreads.text: Every evening Mabel watched the moon rise over the garden wall. "One day," she whispered, "I will see the moonlit garden up close."
spreads.sceneSummary: Mabel looking up at the rising moon.

spreads.text: But the garden looked very big at night, and Mabel felt a little bit wobbly inside. Her friend Hedge the hedgehog came snuffling by.
spreads.sceneSummary: Hedge the hedgehog arrives beside Mabel.

spreads.text: "Being brave means trying, even when you feel wobbly," said Hedge kindly. "Shall we go together?" Mabel took a deep breath and nodded.
spreads.sceneSummary: Hedge and Mabel decide to explore together.

spreads.text: Step by step, paw by paw, they crept along the garden path. The stones were cool and smooth, and the grass smelled sweet.
spreads.sceneSummary: The two friends walk along the stone path.

spreads.text: Pop, pop, pop! Tiny lights blinked on all around them. "Glow-worms!" laughed Hedge. Mabel giggled. Being brave felt warm and fizzy.
spreads.sceneSummary: Glow-worms light up around the friends.

spreads.text: By the pond, a frog sang a slow, sleepy song. The water shone like a silver plate, and the moon smiled down at them.
spreads.sceneSummary: A frog sings by the moonlit pond.

spreads.text: Mabel climbed the tallest flowerpot all by herself. From the top she could see the whole garden, soft and silver in the moonlight.
spreads.sceneSummary: Mabel on top of a flowerpot looking out.

spreads.text: "I was brave!" said Mabel proudly. "You were," said Hedge, "and I was brave too, because we were brave together."
spreads.sceneSummary: Mabel and Hedge smile at each other.

spreads.text: Back under the apple tree, Mabel snuggled into her mossy bed. The moon shone gently through the leaves. Goodnight, brave little Mabel.
spreads.sceneSummary: Mabel asleep in her mossy bed.

blocks.text: Nell Ashby writes gentle bedtime stories about small animals and big feelings. She lives by the sea with a very sleepy cat.
